incident-bot: Incident created: Elevated 5xx error rates and gateway timeouts observed across inference gateway. Paging on-call: @oncall_alex :rotating_light:

oncall_alex: seeing spikes on the dashboards, p50 up ~200ms, p95 spiking to 1.8s and 502/504 counts rising. Which stack is owning prefix/KV cache today?

sre_maya: Runtime team owns prefix cache. I'm looking at kv metrics now — eviction rate jumped ~75x at 10:12 UTC. Also seeing a lot of cache miss fanout to storage.

eng-runtime: Confirmed — one of the prefix shards started evicting aggressively after a compaction. There's evidence of a bad checksum on a small set of keys causing repeated refetches.

pm_jordan: Is there confirmed customer impact? Any major customers affected?

support_lina: Support is seeing a surge of 502 errors for a handful of paying customers in EU region, some latency-sensitive features failing. Logged tickets: 3 high-priority.

oncall_alex: Priority: live mitigation first. What are quick rollbacks? Can we bypass prefix cache for the problematic shard?

eng-runtime: We can set a bypass flag at the routing layer for the shard range, which forces read-through to the durable store and disables prefix aggregation. That will reduce the KV-serving CPU pressure but will increase storage reads.

sre_maya: Storage is already seeing a jump. If we flip bypass globally we risk overloading storage -> 503s. Suggest targeted bypass for the top 3 hot prefixes.+ throttle fanout.

infra-bot: Alert: storage read ops +240% since 10:12 UTC. New write-back queue depth rising.

eng-runtime: Proposed mitigations: 1) throttle prefix fanout to 8 concurrency (was 64) 2) set routing bypass for shard-12 range 3) temporarily disable prefetching on gateway 4) roll a micropatch to fix checksum rejection to stop re-inserting invalid entries.

oncall_alex: Execute 1-3 now. Coordinate 4 as follow-up. Who will apply throttle?

sre_maya: I'll apply fanout throttle at the gateway layer (rate limiter). Doing it now: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/ratelimit -d '{"name":"prefix-fanout","concurrency":8}'`

eng-runtime: I'll flip routing bypass for shard-12. Command: `routesctl set-bypass --shard 12 --enable` — applying in 3..2..1

eng-runtime: ✅ bypass applied to shard-12. Monitoring.

support_lina: Error rates for affected customers reduced from ~40% 502 to ~12% within 90s — they report partial recovery.

infra-bot: Metric update: storage reads back to +60% (from +240%). Gateway 5xx rate reduced 55% relative to peak.

pm_jordan: Good. Any risk of data inconsistency or correctness impact from bypass?

eng-runtime: Bypass forces read-through, so results are authoritative. Prefetch / caching semantics change (no prefix aggregation), but responses should be correct. We need to watch tail latency.

oncall_alex: Next: schedule a controlled rollout to disable prefetching for the whole region if checksums keep failing. Also need a handoff doc for follow-up triage.

sre_maya: Capturing logs for the suspected keys. Sample from shard-12 logs: ```
[10:11:58] PV: checksum_mismatch key=usr:vec:7f3a
[10:11:58] KV: eviction_triggered reason=ttl_mismatch key=usr:vec:7f3a
[10:12:01] Prefetch: miss -> refetch -> store_get
[10:12:02] Prefetch: miss -> refetch -> store_get
[10:12:03] Retry loop detected, client_id=router-34
```

eng-runtime: The micropatch to accept lenient checksum for that key family is ready but needs CI. I'll cut a canary and push to shard-12 host group after we stabilize.

support_lina: Customer tickets updated: most customers back to normal; one still seeing intermittent 504s. I'm adding them to high-priority follow-up.

oncall_alex: Can we set a temporary 5xx alert suppression for noisy symptoms while we do mitigation to avoid pagers? Keep page if errors > 20% of baseline.

sre_maya: I'll set a narrow suppression window for shard-12 alerts for 30m. `/incident suppress --metric gateway_5xx --scope shard:12 --duration 30m --threshold 20%`

infra-bot: Suppression applied by oncall?maria — note: suppression created (id: sup-5632).

oncall_alex: Handoff notes for next oncall (copy to postmortem): root cause suspected corrupted prefix entries causing eviction storms and repeated refetch loops. Mitigations applied: throttle fanout, shard bypass, disable prefetch for shard, suppression. Follow-ups: full checksum audit, micropatch rollout to accept/repair checksum, add circuit-breaker on refetch loops, add alert for eviction-rate-spike.

pm_jordan: Also include customer impact summary and timeline for SRE postmortem.

sre_maya: Timeline snippet: `10:11 UTC - eviction spike on shard-12; 10:12 UTC - 5xx surge; 10:13 UTC - throttling applied; 10:13:30 UTC - route bypass applied; 10:15 UTC - error rate down 55%; 10:40 UTC - suppressed noisy pages`.

eng-runtime: Starting canary patch to repair checksum on one host in shard-12: `deployctl canary --app prefix-service --shard 12 --hosts 1 --image prefix-repair:v2` — will monitor for anomalies.

oncall_alex: If canary looks good, schedule rollout. If not, revert and escalate to oncall-rotations.

support_lina: I'll prepare an update for impacted customers: root cause and temporary mitigations, ETA for full fix (TBD).

eng-runtime: Canary running. Early signs: no repeat refetch loop on patched host after 5m.

infra-bot: Metric update at 10:20 UTC: gateway_5xx decreased to 18% of peak; storage read ops trending down.

oncall_alex: Thanks everyone. I'm closing the immediate pager. Handoff to SRE and Runtime for post-incident triage and postmortem. Please add links to logs and tickets in the handoff doc. :white_check_mark:

sre_maya: Adding notes to incident tracker. Assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime (checksum audit) and infra (prefetch circuit-breaker).

eng-runtime: Acknowledge and will own checksum audit + patch rollout.

support_lina: Filing customer comms draft, will send after PM review.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). Reference: 1952468100.
